title: Selector Launches AI-Powered Multi-Cloud Observability Solution, Closing Network-to-Cloud Visibility Gap
summary: Selector expanded its platform with AI-powered multi-cloud observability capabilities enabling organizations to correlate signals across hybrid infrastructure. The solution unifies telemetry from cloud, network, and infrastructure into a shared intelligence layer using patented data ingestion and ML engines for deterministic root cause analysis across domains.

title: Exaforce Raises $125M Series B for Agentic Security Operations Platform
summary: Exaforce secured $125M Series B funding valued at $725M from HarbourVest, Peak XV, Mayfield, Khosla Ventures, and Seligman Ventures. The agentic SOC platform uses autonomous AI agents called Exabots to handle detection, triage, investigation, and response across cloud and SaaS environments without relying on traditional SIEM rules.

title: Dynatrace Intelligence: Fusing Deterministic AI with Agentic AI for Autonomous Operations
summary: Dynatrace Intelligence combines deterministic AI grounded in real-time causal context with agentic AI for supervised autonomous operations. The system showed 12x higher success rates, 3x faster resolution, and 50% lower token costs versus LLM-only approaches; integrates with ServiceNow for incident prevention automation.

title: Honeycomb Advances Observability for AI-Powered Software Development with Metrics GA and MCP Expansions
summary: Honeycomb announced general availability of Honeycomb Metrics and expanded Model Context Protocol integrations for AI agents as primary consumers of production software. Promotional pricing for Metrics at $2 per 1,000 time series per month through June 2026; Pipeline Intelligence automates telemetry configuration at scale.

title: OpenTelemetry Graduates as CNCF Project, Standardizing Vendor-Neutral Observability
summary: CNCF announced OpenTelemetry's graduation as a stable vendor-neutral framework for standardizing metrics, logs, and traces collection and processing. The project gained momentum observing AI workloads, with JavaScript and Python API packages surpassing 1.36B and 1.3B downloads respectively; widely adopted by Alibaba, Anthropic, Bloomberg, and others.

title: Honeycomb Releases Second Edition of Observability Engineering, Rewritten for AI Era
summary: Honeycomb published Observability Engineering: Achieving Production Excellence, 2nd Edition—almost entirely rewritten by Majors, Fong-Jones, Miranda, and Parker. Covers why AI-generated code validation in production is unsafe, how shipping faster paradoxically slows learning, and includes chapters from practitioners at the frontier of agentic AI operations.

title: Claude Enterprise-Managed Auth for MCP Connectors: Zero-Touch Agent Access via Okta
summary: Anthropic shipped enterprise-managed authorization for MCP connectors on June 18, 2026, allowing IT admins to provision integrations once through Okta. Employees inherit access automatically on first Claude login—no OAuth queues or per-user consent screens needed. Implementation uses the open ID-JAG (Identity JWT Authorization Grant) standard adopted by IETF OAuth Working Group in September 2025.

title: Claude Managed Agents Now Support Self-Hosted Sandboxes and Private MCP Tunnel Access
summary: Anthropic expanded Claude Managed Agents with self-hosted sandboxes and MCP tunnels to address enterprise deployment where organizations want autonomous agents but cannot allow execution environments or internal systems to leave their security perimeter. Self-hosted sandboxes allow tool execution to run on customer-controlled infrastructure or managed providers like Cloudflare, Daytona, Modal, and Vercel.

title: Code Execution with MCP: Building More Efficient AI Agents
summary: Code execution with MCP enables agents to use context more efficiently by loading tools on demand, filtering data before it reaches the model, and executing complex logic in a single step. This approach applies established software engineering patterns to agents, allowing them to interact with MCP servers more efficiently through familiar programming constructs.

title: AI in IT Operations (AIOps) 2026: 12 Best Tools to Automate Your NOC
summary: Practical survey of leading AIOps platforms spanning full-stack observability with embedded AI, pure-play correlation specialists, and automation-first vendors. Alert noise remains the defining operational problem as environments scale across on-premises, cloud, and containerized workloads. Platform selection requires matching architecture to existing operational stack to avoid integration debt.

title: Claude Code Updates: Improved MCP Reliability, OAuth Retries, and 37% CPU Reduction
summary: Claude Code 2.1.191 improves MCP reliability and OAuth retries, adds /rewind command to restore prior context before /clear, and reduces CPU use during streaming by approximately 37%. Background agents now persist across task transitions without restart, and background agent auth automatically reconnects on 401/403 responses.

title: Rise of Agentic AI in NetOps: When Networks Start Managing Themselves
summary: Cisco reports 165,000+ agentic workflows executed in the last 30 days, validating that governed automation is production-live, not theoretical. Gartner forecasts 70% enterprise adoption of agentic AI in infrastructure operations by 2029. Safe first wins focus on triage, validation, RF optimization, and approval-gated remediation—not blind config pushes. Requires cross-domain telemetry, controller-level tool access, and hard policy guardrails before expanding autonomy.

title: Itential Launches FlowAI as Agentic Ops Come to the Fore
summary: Itential announced FlowAI, a governance-backed agentic orchestration platform for infrastructure operations, with general availability July 1, 2026. The three-layer architecture separates agentic reasoning, deterministic execution, and integration/connectivity to enable production-ready autonomous infrastructure operations while maintaining human control—addressing enterprise demand for safe autonomous network and infrastructure agents.

title: Cisco Cloud Control: AgenticOps Platform Enters Controlled Availability
summary: Cisco Cloud Control, unveiled at Cisco Live on June 2, 2026, is a unified platform for humans and AI agents to manage, monitor and defend critical IT infrastructure, delivering a single view across networking, security, compute, observability, and collaboration through one login with shared data layer. Customers can build applications and agents using natural language through Cloud Control Studio, with connectivity to 50+ third-party platforms via native connectors or MCP.

title: HPE Expands Self-Driving Networks Across Edge, Campus, Data Center
summary: HPE announced integration of HPE Networking CX switching with HPE Mist, adding AI-native visibility, zero-touch provisioning, wired assurance and layer 2 access, plus HPE Marvis AI-powered self-driving capabilities for HPE Aruba Central including autonomous wired port remediation. An agentic AI-powered root-cause analysis engine continuously reasons across telemetry and leverages contextual graph data to deliver precise root cause analysis and actionable remediation in the data center network.

title: Arista Networks Announces 7060XE7 Series for Rack-Scale AI Infrastructure
summary: Arista Networks announced the 7060XE7 Series on June 9, 2026, a new portfolio of 1.6T networking platforms designed for rack-scale AI infrastructure. The series includes Smart AI software with dynamic and cluster load balancing to optimize traffic distribution, multipath reliable connection support to prevent link flaps from stalling workloads, and congestion management for granular network health visibility across AI deployments.

title: HPE Discover 2026: Self-Driving Networks and AI Data Center Switching Integration
summary: HPE Discover 2026 marks a milestone in post-Juniper integration with tangible examples of technology integration across switching, operations, automation, and security, including Mist capabilities for Aruba hardware, Marvis automation within Aruba Central, and unified management for AI networking fabrics. New switching hardware includes Juniper QFX5252 for AMD Helios and QFX5140 for inference clusters, officially integrating Juniper into HPE's unified AI networking strategy.

title: Networking Predictions 2026: From Automation Experiments to Agent-Driven Operations
summary: Itential's Head of AI & Developer Relations outlines how 2026 marks the shift from fragmented automation efforts into agent-driven, orchestrated systems. The post details production-ready implementation of MCP, agents, A2A protocols, and orchestration—moving beyond traditional scripting to intent-driven infrastructure where network engineers describe outcomes in natural language rather than writing hundreds of lines of custom code.

title: CrowdStrike Unveils Continuous Identity for AI Agents
summary: CrowdStrike announced Continuous Identity for AI Agents, a new identity security control plane that replaces static policies and standing privileges with continuous, risk-aware authorization. Every AI agent receives cryptographically verifiable identity based on SPIFFE standard, with access evaluated in real-time based on agent ownership, caller identity, and device risk posture. The capability, powered by SGNL technology acquisition, dynamically grants/denies/revokes access and eliminates standing privileges entirely.

title: HPE Brings Agentic AI Into Production with NVIDIA, Delivering Security, Governance, Scale, and Sovereignty
summary: HPE announced expansions to its AI Factory with NVIDIA at HPE Discover 2026, adding NVIDIA Vera CPU, Blackwell GPUs, Spectrum-X Ethernet, BlueField-3 DPUs, and ConnectX-8 SuperNICs with integrated confidential computing and agentic AI governance. Private Cloud AI now scales to 256 GPUs with shared KV cache and multi-node inferencing, with token cost optimization and governance features available July 2026.

title: Arista Introduces Next-Generation 1.6Terabit Portfolio for AI Fabrics
summary: Arista unveiled the 7060XE7 Series, a portfolio of 1.6T networking platforms designed as rack-scale AI infrastructure foundations with support for air, liquid, and hybrid-cooled environments. The series integrates Broadcom Tomahawk 6 silicon and supports diverse accelerators including AMD MI Series XPUs, enabling scale-up and scale-out AI fabrics with deterministic latency and deep buffering for thousands of GPUs.

title: NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet Switches Speed Up Networks for Meta and Oracle
summary: NVIDIA announced Spectrum-X Ethernet adoption by Meta and Oracle for giga-scale AI infrastructure. Meta integrates Spectrum Ethernet into FBOSS for Facebook's open switching platform to accelerate AI training efficiency. Oracle deploying Spectrum-X with Vera Rubin architecture for giga-scale AI factories. Spectrum-X achieves 95% data throughput with congestion control versus 60% for off-the-shelf Ethernet at scale.

summary: OpenAI is postponing the general release of GPT-5.6 in compliance with government request, instead rolling out three separate models: Sol (strongest), Terra (everyday work), and Luna (fastest/cheapest). The Trump administration will approve access customer-by-customer during the staggered rollout, giving federal officials control over adoption timing. This represents a watershed shift in how frontier model releases interface with national security review.

title: Anthropic Forced to Globally Disable Fable 5 and Mythos 5 Under Export Control Directive
summary: Anthropic suspended access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models on June 12 following a U.S. export control directive prohibiting use by anyone who is not a U.S. national. The government cited a report of an exploit that could bypass safety guardrails and trick the model into identifying critical infrastructure vulnerabilities. Anthropic shut down access globally within hours with no warning and no backup plan, creating immediate disruptions for international researchers and enterprises.

title: Zhipu AI Releases GLM-5.2 Open-Source Alternative; Rio 3.5 Outperforms Closed-Source Models on Terminal Benchmarks
summary: Zhipu AI released GLM-5.2 under MIT license with a 1-million-token context window, providing developers a high-capacity localized alternative to closed-source APIs. IplanRIO published Rio 3.5 Open 397B on Hugging Face, achieving competitive Terminal-Bench 2.1 scores and outperforming DeepSeek V4 Pro on code execution. This reflects accelerating momentum toward sovereign, self-hosted deployment frameworks as regulatory disruption to proprietary APIs drives enterprise workload migration.

summary: Verizon CTO Yago Tenorio shared recent progress on using GenAI and training AI agents as part of the carrier's bid for 'Level 4' network autonomy. The deployment demonstrates practical agentic AI moving into operational network tasks, signaling maturation of autonomous network capabilities beyond pilot trials.

title: Lumen Technologies Deploys Ciena Blue Planet AI Agents for Network Operations Automation
summary: Lumen Technologies is adopting Ciena's Blue Planet AI agents across parts of Lumen's network operations to enhance process efficiency and service delivery quality, targeting automation of complex workflows in Lumen's large-scale fiber backbone and edge infrastructure. This deployment reflects the broader industry push toward AI-driven operations support systems.

title: Singtel Receives Up to $28M Government Funding for Multi-Year AI Transformation Programme
summary: Singtel Singapore will receive up to $28 million from Digital Industry Singapore (DISG) for a multi-year AI transformation programme covering AI talent, governance, technology architecture, implementation work and workforce redesign. The first phase focuses on developing a roadmap and operating plan to become an AI-native telco and deploying advanced agentic AI and ML capabilities across all business units.

title: Bell Canada Expands AI Data Centre in Saskatchewan with Cerebras and CoreWeave Partnership
summary: Bell announced a major expansion of Bell AI Fabric through a partnership with the Government of Saskatchewan to develop a new 300 MW purpose-built AI data centre near Regina that will significantly expand Canada's sovereign AI compute capacity. Cerebras and CoreWeave are secured as tenants, with Cerebras providing wafer-scale AI technology for inference and training, while CoreWeave delivers NVIDIA GPU-based compute.

title: SK Hynix Seeks $29 Billion With US Listing to Fund AI Boom
summary: South Korea's SK Hynix completed a blockbuster $29.4 billion US IPO, cementing its position as the top supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for AI data centers. The listing reflects aggressive capital deployment in AI compute infrastructure and the consolidation of memory chip supply chains around frontier AI buildout.

title: Enterprise AI moves from pilot to production in 2026, but gaps in governance and talent persist
summary: Deloitte and NVIDIA surveys show worker access to AI rose 50% in 2025 and agentic AI adoption is accelerating, yet only 20% of companies have mature governance models. Talent shortages remain the biggest adoption barrier across industries as organizations move from experimentation to production deployment.

title: AI News Today June 25 2026: 15 Biggest Stories
summary: Google launched Gemini 2.5 Pro with Deep Think reaching 82.4% on GPQA Diamond and 94.1% on HumanEval+, resetting science reasoning benchmarks. Stanford AI Index 2026 reveals three macro trends: AI progress accelerating with capabilities commodifying in months, frontier training costs creating compute oligopoly concentration, and public trust declining amid concerns about accuracy and job displacement.

title: AI Adoption Makes Real-Time, Streaming Data Central to Enterprise Operations
summary: ISG's 2026 Buyers Guides show enterprises increasingly adopting real-time data processing as foundational for AI-enabled automation. Real-time data evolved from niche to core operational component as agentic systems require immediate decision-making on live business events; ISG expects 75%+ of enterprises to adopt standard streaming architectures by 2028.

title: Global Conference on AI, Security and Ethics 2026
summary: UNIDIR's Global Conference on AI, Security and Ethics 2026 convened diplomats, policymakers, academia, and industry to examine AI's implications for international peace and security. With AI development actively shaping national and regional security environments, participants recognized the need for shared understandings, coordinated approaches, and cross-border cooperation on governance.

title: LogicMonitor Publishes AI Workload Observability as Critical ITOps Priority
summary: LogicMonitor published June 17 that AI workload observability helps ITOps teams monitor AI services and reduce blind spots toward Autonomous IT. Edwin AI helps teams move from signal to action by tracking AI workload performance across infrastructure and user experience layers.

title: New Relic Launches AI Coding Observability Open-Source Feature
summary: New Relic released New Relic AI Coding Observability, an open-source observability solution designed for AI-assisted software development. The tool extends production-grade monitoring into the coding phase to govern, optimize, and audit AI usage across the development lifecycle.

title: Dynatrace AI-Guided Troubleshooting Enters Limited Availability with Explainable AI Focus
summary: Chronosphere introduced AI-Guided Troubleshooting capabilities including Suggestions and Investigation Notebooks in limited availability, emphasizing causal reasoning over pattern-spotting. The company plans full general availability in 2026 and released Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server immediately for direct AI workflow integration.

title: New Relic Expands Azure and GitHub Marketplace Integrations at Microsoft Build 2026
summary: New Relic announced double-digit growth in committed bookings through Microsoft Azure Marketplace over the past 12 months. The company positioned observability as agentic AI context for developer workflows and operations agents, integrating deeper with Azure and GitHub Copilot.

title: Data Center Automation: What's New and What Works in 2026
summary: Explores granular, predictive automation across power delivery, cooling, and operations rather than just generative AI. Covers orchestrated electrical power management systems (EPMS) and intelligent PDU coordination for rack-level power capping and workload prioritization in data centers facing electricity constraints.

title: Zscaler Expands Zero Trust SASE With ZAgent Framework for AI-Era Administration
summary: Zscaler introduced the ZAgent framework at Zenith Live 2026 to automate SASE administration and extend zero trust to unmanaged devices, B2B partners, and multi-cloud workloads. The framework uses natural language prompts for management tasks, while automated micro-segmentation within Kubernetes prevents lateral threat movement without code changes. This addresses legacy SASE's firewall/VPN limitations that expose apps and complicate operations in AI-driven threat environments.

title: Zero Trust for AI Agents: SASE Vendors Race to Secure Non-Human Users
summary: SASE providers Versa Networks, Cisco, and Palo Alto are addressing a fundamental shift: agentic AI will introduce non-human identities predicted to outnumber human users by 80-to-1 or higher, but platforms were not built to secure this new class of users. Versa is extending zero-trust to its Verbo agent at the execution layer, ensuring actions are verified with human users before execution. This reflects a strategic pivot across the SASE ecosystem to handle autonomous agent authentication and authorization.

title: Zscaler Announces AI-Guardian Project and Platform Integrations for Enterprise AI Security
summary: Zscaler announced new AI- and agent-focused capabilities with integrations with Oasis Security, Radiant Logic, and Gigamon to strengthen identity governance and observability across complex hybrid environments. The announcements at Zenith Live 2026 demonstrate vendor consolidation around identity governance and observability as critical foundations for securing distributed AI workloads and agents within zero-trust architectures.

title: Honeycomb Releases Second Edition of Observability Engineering for AI-First Operations
summary: Honeycomb announced the second edition of 'Observability Engineering: Achieving Production Excellence,' updated to reflect that AI agents are now both producers and consumers of observability data in production systems. The revised edition, co-authored by founder Charity Majors with Austin Parker (Director of AI Strategy), addresses how observability platforms must be designed for autonomous agent reasoning and debugging.

title: AI-Native 6G Momentum Building at EuCNC Summit: Agentic AI Integration with Standards Framework
summary: Nokia reported findings from EuCNC & 6G Summit 2026 showing accelerating momentum toward AI-native 6G architectures. Key result: agentic AI will be seamlessly integrated into 6G systems, balancing interoperability requirements from standards bodies (3GPP, ETSI) with practical AI innovations. Commercial deployment timeline remains 2030, but research-to-implementation gap is narrowing significantly.

title: AutoCon 5: Network Automation Forum Convenes 200+ Practitioners on AI-Driven Infrastructure Reliability
summary: Packet Pushers covered AutoCon 5 (June 6-10, 2026) in Munich, where network operators and architects discussed SRE, AI-driven infrastructure automation, network monitoring tools, and code-based traffic management. Keynote: 'The SRE of AI: Engineering Network Reliability for the Tokenized Era,' focusing on maintaining service levels and managing distributed systems under AI workloads.

title: Zscaler Expands Zero Trust SASE with ZAgent Framework for AI-Era Security Operations
summary: Zscaler announced significant expansion of its Zero Trust SASE solution with introduction of ZAgent Framework, an orchestration system designed to automate administrative tasks such as configuration and troubleshooting. Administrators interact with the system using natural language prompts. The expansion includes Zero Trust Gateway for GCP, automated microsegmentation for Kubernetes environments to restrict lateral threat movement, and Zero Trust browser options for BYOD devices.

title: Fortinet Introduces FortiSOC: Unified Cloud-Delivered SOC Platform with Agentic AI
summary: Fortinet held exclusive webinar on June 17, 2026 introducing FortiSOC, a new unified, cloud-delivered SOC platform designed to simplify and scale modern security operations. Platform consolidates alert management and automates response workflows using agentic AI, addressing SOC teams' struggle with manual investigation and response processes.

title: FortiBleed: 73,932 Fortinet Firewalls Compromised via Configuration Exfiltration and Credential Hash Cracking
summary: Security researcher Bob Diachenko discovered FortiBleed, a large-scale credential compromise affecting 73,932 Fortinet FortiGate VPN firewalls across 194 countries. Threat actors extracted configuration files from internet-exposed devices, cracked password hashes using 45-GPU clusters via Hashtopolis, and assembled validated credential database. Campaign included 1.16 billion login attempts against FortiGate targets and 2.1 billion attempts against MSSQL servers, impacting organizations including Samsung, Foxconn, Comcast, and AT&T.

title: Data Center Automation: What's New and What Works in 2026
summary: Modern data center automation extends beyond AI hype to deliver policy-led orchestration across power, cooling, physical security and operations. Platforms now coordinate electrical power management systems (EPMS), DCIM, and intelligent PDUs to enforce rack-level power caps and prioritize workloads. This represents a shift from siloed tools to integrated, predictive automation that enables operators to manage core functions in ways that weren't practical before.

title: Verizon taps AI agents for network automation
summary: Verizon is advancing network automation with agentic AI, deploying agents to handle operational tasks with early promising results. The carrier's foundation is the on-premise Verizon Cloud Platform (VCP) hosting virtual and cloud-native network functions, running 60,000 vRAN sites. From early learnings, Verizon emphasizes the industry must focus on security, transparency, and common frameworks for agentic network operations as autonomous agents move into production environments.

title: 2026 Network Outage Report and Internet Health Check
summary: Public cloud network outages increased 14% globally to 87 events week-over-week, with U.S. outages rising 16% to 66. Software-driven failures like Verizon's January network-wide outage reveal vulnerabilities exist inside the network itself, not just geographically. This underscores why observability, automation tooling, and incident response automation are mission-critical for preventing cascading failures across interdependent infrastructure.

title: Zscaler expands Zero Trust SASE with ZAgent Framework for agentic administration
summary: Zscaler introduced the ZAgent Framework at Zenith Live 2026, an agentic AI orchestration layer that automates SASE administration through natural language prompts in the Experience Center. The framework coordinates specialized agents to reduce IT/security resolution time, simplify multi-cloud management, and correlate context across 500 trillion daily signals to improve detection accuracy. The expansion addresses modern attack environments where legacy firewall/VPN-based SASE fails to secure unmanaged devices, supply chains, and distributed workloads.

title: GitHub Agentic Workflows Now in Public Preview
summary: GitHub shipped agentic workflows in public preview, enabling automation of reasoning-based tasks like issue triage, CI failure analysis, and documentation updates via coding agents in GitHub Actions. Workflows are defined in natural language Markdown, compiled to standard Actions YAML, and reuse existing runner groups and policy constraints.

title: Zscaler Expands Zero Trust SASE with ZAgent Framework for Autonomous Operations
summary: Zscaler introduced the ZAgent Framework at Zenith Live 2026 to automate SASE administration through agentic AI, enabling administrators to orchestrate configuration, troubleshooting, and root-cause analysis via natural language prompts. The platform extends Zero Trust protections to unmanaged devices, B2B partners, and multi-cloud workloads with new capabilities including Zero Trust Gateway for GCP, Kubernetes microsegmentation, and endpoint sandbox protection.

title: Elastic brings AI-driven incident investigation to Kubernetes with agentic workflow and MCP-based observability skills
summary: Elastic introduced an agentic Kubernetes investigation workflow that automatically diagnoses incidents the moment an alert fires, with root cause identification and evidence assembly completed before an SRE opens the alert. The MCP-based observability skills close the gap between alert and answer by starting investigation automatically before on-call engineers are paged, reducing the manual triage burden for teams running Kubernetes at scale.

title: Zscaler Expands Zero Trust SASE with ZAgent Framework for Agentic AI Operations
summary: At Zenith Live 2026 on June 10, Zscaler introduced ZAgent Framework that orchestrates agents across the Zero Trust SASE platform to automate administration, configuration, and troubleshooting through natural language prompts. The platform now secures over 750 billion daily transactions and extends to unmanaged devices, B2B partners, and multi-cloud workloads with new Zero Trust browser options for BYOD, B2B connectivity, GCP gateway, and Kubernetes microsegmentation. This positions SASE as a unified control layer for human and machine identities, addressing enterprise demand for single policy engines across AI-agent activity.

title: BlueVoyant Launches BlueVoyant AI Agentic Security Operations Platform
summary: BlueVoyant launched BlueVoyant AI on June 12, an agentic SOC platform available as fully managed service or self-service software, designed for real-time decision-making and automated response during attacks. The platform addresses the sector-wide challenge of alert fatigue and slow triage by applying AI to detection and response workflows, reducing false positives and enabling faster containment. Available in managed and in-house deployment models with 24/7 security operations support.

title: Tata Communications ThreadSpan: AIOps and Network Observability Platform Update
summary: On June 12, Tata Communications published technical guidance on AIOps combining AI, machine learning, and big data to automate IT operations and reduce alert fatigue. ThreadSpan platform enables proactive operations through real-time visibility, anomaly detection, and automated remediation, with enterprise benefits including predictive capacity planning, unified hybrid cloud visibility, faster MTTR, and reduced manual intervention across observability baselines and phased automation strategies.

title: Atlassian integrates Honeycomb, Coralogix, and Lansweeper into Jira Service Management for AIOps workflows
summary: Atlassian announced new integrations bringing specialized telemetry from Honeycomb's high-cardinality observability, Coralogix's log analytics, and Lansweeper's asset discovery directly into Jira Service Management, enabling faster root cause analysis and reduced swivel-chair work by connecting observability data to the Teamwork Graph and Rovo agents via MCP server.

title: ServiceNow expands Autonomous Workforce with AIOps and SRE specialists launching June 2026
summary: ServiceNow announced an expansion of its Autonomous Workforce platform at Knowledge 2026, including new AIOps specialist that autonomously detects anomalies, correlates events, and triggers remediation, plus SRE specialist handling incident triage and postmortem documentation end-to-end, with IT AI specialists expected in June 2026.

title: Verizon taps AI agents for network automation
summary: Verizon is deploying agentic AI for network automation tasks with early positive results, running workloads on its on-premise Verizon Cloud Platform that hosts vRAN and 5G core functions. The carrier emphasizes industry focus on security, transparency, and common frameworks for safe agentic network operations.

title: Cybersecurity Weekly News Roundup (June 6 – June 12, 2026)
summary: Security landscape analysis covering the week ending 6/12/2026 highlighting how AI-driven cyber attacks, ransomware, and security automation have become standard attack vectors. Organizations are increasing investment in threat detection systems, cloud security products, zero trust principles, and security automation technologies in response to evolving threats.

title: Cisco Cloud Control Launch: Unified AgenticOps Platform Available in Controlled Availability
summary: Cisco announced Cloud Control in Controlled Availability as of June 2, 2026, with global availability in July. The platform unifies networking, security, observability, and infrastructure management under a single control plane with an AI Canvas for real-time investigation and remediation by human operators and AI agents working from shared telemetry.

title: The Biggest Announcements From Cisco Live 2026
summary: Cisco Live 2026 emphasized autonomous infrastructure across networking, security, and cloud. Cloud Control emerged as the flagship announcement, repositioning network operations from static management toward AI-driven autonomous execution with AgenticOps as the operational model where AI agents manage infrastructure across multiple domains.

title: Itential Brings Governed AI Agents to Enterprise Infrastructure with FlowAI General Availability
summary: Itential announced FlowAI general availability at Cisco Live US 2026 (June 1), delivering production-ready agentic orchestration with enterprise governance and security controls. FlowAI enables infrastructure teams to build and deploy AI agents with built-in audit trails, role-based access control, and deterministic execution guardrails validated across telecom, financial services, and utilities.

summary: Zscaler introduced the ZAgent Framework at Zenith Live 2026 that orchestrates platform agents to automate SASE configuration, troubleshooting, and policy work through natural-language prompts instead of legacy consoles. title: Zero Trust for AI Agents: SASE Vendors Race to Secure Non-Human Users
summary: SASE providers including Versa Networks, Cisco, and Palo Alto are implementing zero-trust controls for agentic AI entities, as traditional security systems built for human actors cannot scale to protect an estimated 80-to-1 ratio of non-human identities. title: Palo Alto Networks Addresses Cortex XSIAM and XSOAR Vulnerabilities in CommvaultSecurityIQ Integration

Joint solutions for autonomous infrastructure operations integrate Red Hat Ansible, IBM Bob, Instana, Terraform and Vault into ServiceNow IT workflows to detect and remediate issues before they impact business, with availability expected H2 2026.

The framework allows communication with external agents via Model Context Protocol (MCP) across multi-vendor, multi-domain networks. The enhancement, commercially available by end of 2026, addresses operator concerns around explainability, trust, and risk in production environments.

title: MCP Python and C# SDKs updated June 11, 2026—release candidate 2026-07-28 introduces stateless core and horizontal scaling
summary: The official MCP Python and C# SDKs were updated June 11, 2026, as maintainers continue iteration on SDK tier conformance. The MCP 2026-07-28 release candidate introduces a stateless protocol core, extensions framework for Tasks and MCP Apps, OAuth hardening, and formal deprecation policy to enable horizontal scaling on commodity HTTP infrastructure without session persistence.

title: Blue Yonder advances autonomous supply chain operations with multi-agent coordination and Nvidia partnership
summary: Blue Yonder announced warehouse ops, logistics ops, and inventory ops agents now performing autonomous actions alongside humans, evolved from monitoring and analytics. The company is developing agent-to-agent interaction patterns to solve end-to-end supply chain problems in labs, with planned customer deployment rollout. This demonstrates multi-agent orchestration moving from proof-of-concept to production operations at scale.

title: Firecrawl MCP adoption surges 35% month-over-month as OAuth and authentication patterns mature
summary: Firecrawl reported 35% MCP usage growth in the last month, with Google Trends showing clear resurgence in MCP search interest through H1 2026. MCP's native OAuth and delegated authentication capabilities are driving renewed adoption by addressing authentication complexity that CLI-only approaches cannot replicate. This signals MCP transitioning from experimental local tooling to production multi-agent infrastructure.

title: agnt8x (EightX Labs) launches public platform for agent recruitment, orchestration, and Agent Manifest specification
summary: EightX Labs opened agnt8x, a public platform for recruiting, onboarding, operating, and monetizing AI agents with a builder marketplace, unified audit trail, and multi-agent conductor. The platform published Agent Manifest (EAM) v0.1 under Apache 2.0 license. This provides vendors-neutral management layer for teams scaling multiple agents across providers, reducing vendor lock-in and improving compliance governance.

title: ManageEngine OpManager Nexus Adds Native gNMI and OpenConfig Streaming Telemetry Support
summary: OpManager Nexus now natively supports gRPC Network Management Interface (gNMI) and OpenConfig streaming telemetry for real-time network visibility. Push-based network data collection directly from infrastructure enables enterprises to identify and address anomalies before services are impacted. Vendor-neutral support spans Cisco, Juniper Networks, Arista, Nokia, and Huawei.

title: AutoCon 5 Munich Confirms Network Automation Forum's Practitioner-First Focus for June 2026
summary: AutoCon 5 in Munich in June 2026, organized by the Network Automation Forum, combines hands-on technical workshops with a multi-day conference program featuring keynotes and community-driven content. The event addresses challenges including slow automation adoption, lack of standardized frameworks, and integration of AI/ML into network operations, targeting network engineers, automation engineers, and NetDevOps practitioners.

title: Zscaler Expands Zero Trust SASE with ZAgent Framework for Agentic AI Operations
summary: Zscaler unveiled an expanded zero-trust SASE platform with a new ZAgent Framework that lets administrators manage the system through natural-language prompts, orchestrating platform agents to automate configuration, troubleshooting and policy work. Key additions include Zero Trust browser options for BYOD, Zero Trust B2B connectivity, endpoint sandbox, a Zero Trust Gateway for Google Cloud Platform, and Kubernetes microsegmentation to reduce lateral movement across VMs and containers. The company now secures over 750 billion daily transactions.

title: Versa Brings Zero Trust Controls to AI Agent Actions with Patent-Pending MCP Architecture
summary: Versa released a patent-pending MCP architecture that verifies agent-generated actions before execution, giving operators policy control and human approval over AI-driven operations, integrated with the VersaONE Universal SASE Platform. The solution addresses the trust problem where single user prompts trigger multiple underlying steps across network and security systems; administrators define policies that determine which agent actions execute automatically, require human approval, or are blocked based on user identity, role, system context, action type, and risk level.

title: SASE Vendors Race to Secure Non-Human Users as Agentic AI Floods Enterprise Networks
summary: Agentic AI will introduce an infinite number of non-human entities trying to access networks, with traditional security systems built to protect against human actors and their finite numbers. SASE providers Versa Networks, Cisco, Palo Alto and others are scrambling to get defenses in place before the proliferation of AI agents intensifies the complexity. Gartner noted that SASE providers would need to adapt given agentic AI has created a new class of users that their platforms were not built to secure.

title: Arista Introduces 1.6T Ethernet Portfolio for Rack-Scale AI Fabrics with Liquid-Cooled Switching
summary: Arista announced the 7060XE7 Series, a portfolio of 1.6 Terabit Ethernet platforms designed as rack-scale AI infrastructure foundations, addressing extreme density, power, and thermal requirements with support for air and liquid-cooled deployments. The systems include AI-specific EOS features for congestion management, dynamic load balancing, and collective communication patterns, with 64-port air-cooled availability in Q4 2026 and liquid-cooled/128-port configurations in early 2027.

title: Nvidia Data Center Networking Revenue Hits Record $14.8B on NVLink and Spectrum-X Ethernet Ramp
summary: Nvidia reported record data center networking revenue of $14.8 billion, up 199% year-over-year and 35% sequentially, driven by NVLink compute fabric for GB200/GB300 systems and growth in Ethernet and InfiniBand platforms. This reflects networking's emergence as critical infrastructure within hyperscale AI data centers, with customers prioritizing high-speed fabric performance alongside GPU deployment.

title: OpenTelemetry Launches 'Blueprints' Initiative to Simplify Enterprise Observability Adoption
summary: OpenTelemetry introduced a 'Blueprints' initiative to reduce complexity of deploying observability systems at scale, providing prescriptive guidance, architectural patterns, and reference implementations for consistent adoption across Kubernetes, infrastructure, applications, and cloud-native environments. The announcement reflects mounting feedback from enterprises struggling with operational overhead including SDK configuration, Collector deployment patterns, semantic conventions, and consistency across distributed systems.

title: The Next Evolution of AIOps: Event Intelligence Solutions Reach Slope of Enlightenment
summary: On June 2, Gartner positioned Event Intelligence Solutions on the Slope of Enlightenment in its 2026 Hype Cycle for Infrastructure & Operations. The industry is moving beyond data collection and insight generation toward enabling systems to learn continuously from operational experience. As enterprises pursue Autonomous Operations and Agentic AI, operational knowledge is becoming a strategic asset rather than just a tactical capability.

title: DNS-AID launched under Linux Foundation for decentralized AI agent discovery
summary: The Linux Foundation's DNS-AID project enables AI agents and Model Context Protocol servers to use DNS as a global, vendor-neutral directory for publishing, discovering, and verifying one another. Infoblox shipped the first production system on June 3, 2026; Verisign independently published research on June 1 concluding DNS is the right foundation for agent discoverability at internet scale. Gartner forecasts that by 2030, half of AI agent deployment failures will stem from insufficient governance and broken interoperability.

title: The Next Evolution of AIOps: From Event Intelligence to Operational Knowledge
summary: Gartner's 2026 Hype Cycle for Infrastructure & Operations positions Event Intelligence Solutions on the Slope of Enlightenment, signaling a market shift from event collection toward systems that learn continuously from operational experience. The industry is moving beyond monitoring to operational knowledge as the foundation for autonomous operations and agentic AI—a critical distinction for teams evaluating AIOps maturity and governance.

title: What the 2026 Latio Security Operations Market Report Gets Right About the AI SOC
summary: Exaforce earned AI Innovator, SIEM Disruptor, and User Reliability Leader recognition in Latio's 2026 report. The analysis distinguishes between tools that bolt LLM reasoning onto SOAR frameworks versus true AI-native architectures with real-time knowledge graphs built at ingestion—a technical distinction that determines whether automation produces signal or noise at scale.

title: Microsoft launches MXC, an OS-level sandbox for AI agents, with OpenAI and Nvidia already on board
summary: Microsoft introduced Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC)—a policy-driven execution layer built into Windows that enforces OS kernel-level boundaries on what AI agents can access. This addresses the critical security gap of agent containment that has been absent from the industry, with OpenAI and Nvidia already adopting the approach.

title: AI Agents News | June, 2026 (STARTUP EDITION)
summary: June 2026 marks the inflection point where the market shifted from 'Are AI agents real?' to 'Which part of my company gets agentized first?' Coverage includes BCG legitimizing agents as operating models, GitHub positioning coding agents for generation and refactoring, and Databricks emphasizing production-ready evaluation and governance—signaling maturation from demos to operational infrastructure.

title: Daily AI Agent News - Last 7 Days
summary: Recent developments include Aible's NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra support for long-running governed agents (June 4), MetaMask Agent Wallet with mandatory security checks and spending limits (June 8 early access), and agnt8x's public multi-agent orchestration platform with Agent Manifest v0.1 (June 8)—demonstrating practical governance and multi-provider orchestration patterns.

title: The AI Update — June 5, 2026: Agents Are Working, Regulation Is Moving, and the Hype Is Over
summary: Mid-2026 convergence analysis across policy, agents, multimodal tools, and enterprise-grade distribution. Argues that AI is shifting from flashy demos to real business systems and partners—with agentic AI as the dominant theme enabling multi-step workflows and semi-autonomous orchestration at enterprise scale.

title: AutoCon 5 Underway in Munich: Network Automation Forum Convenes 700+ Practitioners for Real-World Automation Workflows
summary: AutoCon 5 conference (June 8-12, 2026) in Munich brings together network automation practitioners sharing production implementations. Key sessions include PlayStation's ops-led automation strategy, NAF Framework updates, gRPC-based network automation (gNMI/gNOI/gNSI), and hands-on workshops on Event-Driven Automation. Itential, Nokia, NetBox Labs, Cisco, Arista, and HPE are major sponsors; Chris Wade (Itential CTO) closes keynote Friday; practical focus on why automation adoption remains below 25% in enterprises despite billions invested.
source: Network Automation Forum / AC5 Program Guide

title: HPE Announces Fully Autonomous, Agentic AIOps Networking with Self-Driving Actions Across Mist and Aruba Central
summary: HPE delivered autonomous networking capabilities enabling networks to detect, diagnose, and resolve issues without human intervention using microservices-based architecture and autonomous agents. New self-driving actions include dynamic capacity optimization, rogue DHCP detection/remediation, real-time DFS, autonomous VLAN remediation, and client roaming optimization. UK Ministry of Justice achieved 75% reduction in service desk tickets managing 15,000 devices; autonomy is configurable with human-in-the-loop option; dual-mode Wi-Fi 7 APs support both HPE Mist and Aruba Central.

title: Zscaler Expands Zero Trust SASE with ZAgent Framework for Natural-Language Administration
summary: Zscaler expanded its Zero Trust SASE offering with a ZAgent Framework that uses software agents to manage SASE administration through natural language prompts, automating configuration, troubleshooting, and operational tasks. The platform now includes a Zero Trust Gateway for Google Cloud Platform enabling consistent, policy-driven security for workload-to-workload traffic, and automated microsegmentation for Kubernetes stops lateral threat movement across VMs and containers with zero code changes.

title: How AI Is Automating IT Operations in 2026
summary: AIOps adoption is accelerating with platforms reducing mean time to resolution by 60% and cutting alert noise by 85% within the first year. Open-source PSA and IT management tools are democratizing access to automation, with smaller IT teams now able to deploy stacks that previously required enterprise budgets. The market is projected to grow from $2.67 billion in 2026 to $11.8 billion by 2034, driven by unsustainable manual operations as cloud sprawl and security tooling multiply system complexity.

title: Nvidia has a radical new AI-RAN plan – a 6G radio unit chip
summary: Nvidia is developing an embedded GPU-accelerator chip targeting 6G radio units (sub-100W design), extending AI-RAN beyond centralized baseband compute into distributed radio access. The move signals Nvidia's intent to influence the full RAN stack and follows established partnerships with Nokia, T-Mobile, and carriers for field-validated AI-RAN trials.

title: Analysis: Nvidia's rumored new 6G AI-RAN – likely features/functions and industry impact
summary: IEEE technical analysis maps likely AI-RAN functions for Nvidia's rumored 6G radio-unit chip: neural channel estimation, real-time beam management for massive MIMO, and spectrum agility. Analysis positions the move as reinforcing AI-native RAN architecture trends while noting practical constraints around cost/power/flexibility versus incumbent radio silicon.

title: AI News Today - June 8, 2026: 16 Biggest Stories
summary: Broad industry roundup covering Microsoft Build 2026 AI infrastructure updates (Foundry model catalog now 11,000+ models), EU AI Act enforcement (August 2, 2026 deadline for high-risk systems), and SpaceX IPO pricing. Provides context on enterprise AI platform consolidation and regulatory timing affecting infrastructure team planning for 2026 deployments.

title: Autonomous Incident Resolution at Hyperscale: An Agentic AI Architecture for Network Operations
summary: Published Jun 8, 2026. Presents an agentic AI architecture for autonomous incident resolution in large-scale network operations using multi-agent orchestration where specialized agents detect, diagnose, and remediate incidents. Deployed in production at a major cloud provider with autonomous resolution rates exceeding 90% for common incident categories while maintaining safety boundaries through hierarchical decomposition, skills-based tool invocation, and progressive autonomy.

title: Silent Failure in LLM Agent Systems: The Entropy Principle and the Inevitable Disorder of Autonomous Agents
summary: Systematic empirical analysis of 40,000+ controlled trials and 100,000+ agent interactions identifying silent failures in LLM agent systems—unexpected deviations under normal conditions routinely misattributed to bugs. Synthesizes 22 intrinsic failure properties across six lifecycle layers: foundation semantics, inter-agent transmission, memory persistence, task execution, feedback correction, and systemic evolution. Critical for operators deploying autonomous agents.

title: When AIOps Become "AI Oops": Subverting LLM-driven IT Operations via Telemetry Manipulation
summary: First security analysis of LLM-based AIOps systems showing how adversaries can manipulate telemetry to mislead autonomous agents into compromising infrastructure. Introduces AIOpsDoom attack (automated reconnaissance + fuzzing + adversarial input generation) and AIOpsShield defense that sanitizes structured telemetry without degrading agent performance. Exposes critical vulnerability in emerging AIOps deployments.

title: OpenTelemetry Launches "Blueprints" Initiative to Simplify Enterprise Observability Adoption
summary: OpenTelemetry introduced a new Blueprints initiative providing prescriptive guidance, architectural patterns, and reference implementations to reduce complexity in large-scale observability deployments. The initiative addresses feedback from enterprises struggling with SDK configuration, Collector deployment patterns, and semantic convention consistency, offering reusable patterns for Kubernetes, infrastructure outside K8s, and centralized telemetry architectures. Adobe, Mastodon, and Skyscanner have already contributed real-world reference implementations demonstrating how blueprint guidance applies at scale.

title: DriveNets Raises $410M Series D to Scale Ethernet AI Fabric and Heterogeneous AI Infrastructure
summary: DriveNets closed a $410M Series D led by Bessemer Venture Partners and Atreides Management, bringing total capital to $1B and valuation to $8.5B. The Israeli networking firm provides disaggregated Ethernet-based AI fabric solutions addressing GPU cluster underutilization due to network bottlenecks. With $1B+ in secured business and cash-flow positive since 2025, the funding scales inventory for multi-vendor heterogeneous AI infrastructure, critical as the networking market for AI server farms approaches $200B by 2030.

title: OpenTelemetry Achieves CNCF Graduated Project Status, Confirming De Facto Observability Standard
summary: The CNCF announced OpenTelemetry's graduation to highest maturity level on May 21, 2026, after passing independent security audits and governance review. With 12,000+ contributors from 2,800+ companies and second-highest project velocity in CNCF (after Kubernetes), OTel standardizes telemetry collection across metrics, logs, traces, and newly-alpha profiles. JavaScript and Python API packages each exceeded 1.3B downloads in trailing 12 months, solidifying vendor-neutral observability as production-ready infrastructure for cloud native and AI workloads.
